text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Shares ended mostly lower after a session dominated by an unsteady performance in New York and caution ahead of monetary policy meetings both here and in the U.S. later in the week. The leading FTSE 100 index finished just off the day's worst levels, down 18.0 points at 4,257.8.

FRANKFURT - Shares were lifted to new records on the back of the dollar's ongoing strength against the mark, but the rally was tempered by caution before a slew of key international economic events. The blue chip DAX-30 index ended the floor session up 27.14 points at an all-time high of 3,062.29 and the IBIS DAX, which tracks screen trade, edged up to 3,064.70.

PARIS - Shares closed lower on profit-taking from historic highs, under the influence of Wall Street's declines, but the blue-chip index remained above the 2,500 level. The blue-chip CAC-40 index fell 8.01 points or 0.32 percent at 2,508.55.

ZURICH - Shares overcame early weakness to end at a new closing record, but still slightly off the all-time high of nearly 4,300 points in the blue-chip SMI. The U.S. dollar's strength, lively buying interest by foreign investors and prospects for low interest rates were seen as factors behind the rise. The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 10.6 points, to 4,282.8 points. The broad SPI was up 8.93 points to 2,737.26.

TOKYO - Stocks ended a cautious session with losses as investors sat back to await an auction of land by a former state-owned railway firm after market hours. Attention was also being paid to movements in the currency market ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Berlin this weekend. The 225-share Nikkei average shed 244.06 points or 1.33 percent to close at 18,085.95.

HONG KONG - Stocks rallied to a strong close as investors anticipated a steady interest rate outlook in the near term and a pick up in market tone following the Chinese New Year holiday. The Hang Seng Index rose 129.28 points to 13,451.07, led by a surge in property stocks. However, turnover fell to HK$8.43 billion compared with HK$9.10 billion on Friday.

SYDNEY - The share market ambled to a just firmer close with the market buoyed by a bank sector boosted by hopes of local interest rate cuts and a U.S. bond market rally. The All Ordinaries index added 3.2 points to 2,426.9. The benchmark indicator spent the most of the day wandering in an eight point range with little inspiration for traders to commit to either side of the market.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial and all-share indices were boosted by a firm rand, but golds slipped on the strength in the currency and a weaker bullion price. Dealers said futures players were active in the market and there was good demand. The overall index rose 37.5 points to 6,713.6, the industrial index gained 58.6 points to 8,061.9 points and the gold index shed 11.0 points to 1,339.0 points.
